analyst_view.overall: Early view: Second-placed Castellón, who visit Valladolid first, have the best defence in the division and have beaten Sporting 4-0 and Tenerife 5-0 at Castalia. Eldense under Javi Calleja host Sabadell first and had lost their last two league games without scoring before their round-13 trip to Las Palmas. Matías Orozco, listed by the site as suspended, should have served his ban at Valladolid.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, almost all of them Castellón's. I stay close to that: Castellón can run up scores at home (4-0, 5-0) but also grind out narrow results, and Eldense have gone two league games without a goal, so the total depends almost entirely on how ruthless the hosts are.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Pablo Hernández's side use the full width of the pitch from back to front and should spend long spells in Eldense's half, which pushes their 5.6 up. Eldense want the ball under Calleja, but at Castalia they are unlikely to keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with 3.1 for Eldense. I lean lower: Eldense have one of the cleaner records in the division (28 yellows and no reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), and Castellón win the ball back through possession and quick recovery rather than by fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and I agree. Castellón will take most of them; Eldense managed 13 at home to Granada but will get far fewer at Castalia. Nothing in the news moves the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Castellón's forwards (Israel Suero six goals, Ousmane Camara four) are efficient and the site already gives them the bulk; I keep the figure until the round-14 news is in.
